check_in_states.question: ready
check_in_states.hint: {name} is bouncing on their toes at the door.
check_in_states.adapt: You keep the warm-up short and let them get stuck in.

check_in_states.question: sleep
check_in_states.hint: {name} yawns twice before taking off their coat.
check_in_states.adapt: You add a longer, gentler warm-up to wake them up.

check_in_states.question: legs
check_in_states.hint: {name} walks in a little stiffly, rubbing a calf.
check_in_states.answer: Calves are tight from the weekend.
check_in_states.adapt: You add some mobility first so the soreness eases.

check_in_states.question: week
check_in_states.hint: {name} keeps checking their phone, jaw tight.
check_in_states.adapt: You talk it through for a minute; their shoulders drop.

approaches.name: Calm
approaches.line: Nice and steady. You're doing exactly what you need to.

approaches.name: Upbeat
approaches.line: Yes! Look at you go! Big energy!

approaches.name: Competitive
approaches.line: Last week's you is right behind. Don't let him catch you.

approaches.name: Informative
approaches.line: This is the bit that builds your aerobic engine. Hold it here.

approach_right.competitive: Jordan grins and digs in. "Not a chance."
approach_right.anxious: Peg's shoulders drop. She breathes out and keeps going.
approach_right.social: They laugh and pick up the rhythm.
approach_right.analytical: They nod. Knowing why makes it easier.

approach_wrong.competitive: Jordan rolls his eyes. Gentle talk bores him.
approach_wrong.anxious: Peg tenses up. Pressure makes her worry she's failing.
approach_wrong.social: They go quiet. The mood dips.
approach_wrong.analytical: They frown. That didn't tell them anything.

encouragement_situations.cue: {name} is labouring now: head down, every stride an effort.
encouragement_situations.right: {name} settles into your calm voice and keeps moving. Pressure would have broken them.
encouragement_situations.wrong: {name} has nothing left for that. They slow to a walk for a few steps.

encouragement_situations.cue: {name} shakes their head and mutters about that last bit.
encouragement_situations.right: Hearing what the work is doing turns {name}'s frustration into focus.
encouragement_situations.wrong: {name} is frustrated, and that didn't touch it. They stay tense.

encouragement_situations.cue: {name} is flying: grinning, light on their feet, looking for more.
encouragement_situations.right: {name} rides the moment and lifts the effort.
encouragement_situations.wrong: {name} was ready for more, and that took the shine off it.

encouragement_usual: {usual} is {name}'s usual, so it half works. But {name} is {state} right now: {best} would have helped more.

minigame_advice.pace: In {exercise}, wait for the marker to reach the green band: it is the effort they should hold, not a guess.
minigame_advice.technique: In {exercise}, watch for the fault to flash up before pressing, then pick the cue that fixes that fault.
minigame_advice.encouragement: In {exercise}, read the cue line before choosing: how {name} looks right now matters as much as their personality.
minigame_advice.effort: In {exercise}, decide from the signal colour: continue on green, stop on red, and on amber follow the block rule.

green.name: Fresh
cues: Light on their feet and chatting.

amber.name: Working
cues: Quiet now, jaw set, working hard.
Sweating and concentrating on every step.

red.name: Overreaching
cues: Gasping, shoulders hunched, stumbling a little.
Wincing on each stride, arms flailing.

peak_feedback.green_push: They were fresh, so pushing was right: extra work, well spent.
peak_feedback.green_hold: They were fresh. Holding back wasted a good chance to train.
peak_feedback.amber_push_right: Working hard in a {block} block is the point. Pushing paid off.
peak_feedback.amber_push_wrong: In a {block} block, amber means bank the work. Pushing just piled on fatigue.
peak_feedback.amber_hold_right: In a {block} block, amber is enough. Holding back kept fatigue down.
peak_feedback.amber_hold_wrong: In a {block} block amber is where gains are made. Holding back cost progress.
peak_feedback.red_hold: They were overreaching. Holding back was the right call.
peak_feedback.red_push: They were already overreaching. Pushing risked injury and added a lot of fatigue.
peak_feedback.missed: No clear call at the key moment. The chance passed.

endurance.weak: Hit the wall at {km} km and walked long stretches.
endurance.strong: Still running smoothly at {km} km while others walked.

pace.weak: Couldn't hold goal pace after halfway.
pace.strong: Held goal pace comfortably through halfway.

strength.weak: Form fell apart over the last 10 km; calves cramped at {km} km.
strength.strong: Strong legs held good form right to the finish.

recovery.weak: Started the race with heavy legs from training.
recovery.strong: Arrived at the start line fresh and rested.

knowledge.weak: Went out far too fast in the first 5 km and paid for it.
knowledge.strong: Ran even splits, exactly as planned.

guidance.endurance: Endurance lags: more easy and long runs.
guidance.pace: Pace lags: tempo runs and intervals, in Build and Peak.
guidance.strength: Strength lags: squats, lunges, step-ups, core.
guidance.recovery: Recovery lags: foam rolling and lighter weeks.
guidance.knowledge: Pacing Knowledge lags: nail the pace coaching.

blocks.base: Build the base: mostly easy and long running, plus strength. Nothing heroic yet; at an amber signal, hold back.
blocks.build: Add quality: tempo runs and intervals raise Pace. Amber is where the gains are; push through it.
blocks.peak: The hardest weeks: the longest runs and race-pace work. Push at amber, but red still means hold back.
blocks.taper: Race week. Cut the load so they arrive fresh; fatigue on race morning costs readiness. Hold back at amber.

advice.no_hard: {exercise} on Hard stops being what it is for. Use Easy or Moderate.
advice.beginner_no_hard: {name} is new to training. {exercise} on Hard risks injury.
advice.taper_no_hard: The taper is for arriving fresh. A Hard {exercise} undoes it.
advice.base_caution_new: {name} has no running base yet. Intervals in the Base block are too much, too soon.
advice.base_caution: Intervals this early help less than building the base first.
advice.kg_heavy: {kg} kg is too heavy for {name} right now (about {fit} kg suits). Form will break down.
advice.kg_light: {kg} kg is light for {name}. It will work, but gently.
advice.met: {name} already has the {attribute} the goal needs. {exercise} will do little.
advice.weather: Rain is forecast; outdoor runs will be cut short without a treadmill.
advice.road_intervals: Intervals on the road loop are imprecise (80% value). A track membership fixes this.
advice.no_long_run: No long run in the plan. It's the most marathon-specific session there is.
advice.too_tiring: This plan adds about {fatigue} fatigue per session. {name} may arrive tired next time.
